citationText: 23. The idea of interlacing preceded the RCA work, however, as historians have pointed out, including Joseph H. Udelson in his The Great Television Race: A History of the American Television Industry 1925–1941 ( University, Alabama : The University of Alabama Press , 1982 ), pp. 67 – 68 , 174 – 175 . Udelson describes Ulises A. Sanabria's triple-interlace system (first disclosed in 1929) which used a scanning disk. Regular broadcasts in the Chicago area began on those standards in 1930.
